sources.title: Groundwater level telemetry, Nagpur district: Maharashtra Groundwater Surveys and Development Agency (GSDA) and CGWB six-hourly resources on the National Water Data Portal
sources.publisher: National Water Informatics Centre (NWIC), Ministry of Jal Shakti

provenance.note: Monthly means of six-hourly telemetry per station, after the shared quality rules; stations placed by coordinates in the IN-GRES unit polygons, not by their district tag.

well_type: Telemetric recorders in GSDA dug wells and piezometers, and CGWB piezometers
aquifer: Not published per station on this portal; India-WRIS lists the ten CGWB piezometers in the district as semi-confined, 23.5 to 69.5 m deep
cadence_note: Telemetric recorders reading every six hours; shown as monthly means. Months with no reading that passed the quality rules are absent, not zero.

wells.name: Khairi (Kh)
wells.quality_note: The level steps from about 34 m to about 9 m below ground between April and June 2023, and back to about 31 m in February 2024. The portal does not explain either step, so compare readings only within each stretch.

wells.name: Paradsinga_1
wells.quality_note: From July 2025 this station's readings drift above ground level: six monthly means are below zero (July 2025, and May, June, July, August and September 2026). The portal gives no reason, so these months should not be read as water standing above the ground.
